scalars.scalar_value: Five (5) years of professional experience teaching at a higher education institution and/or serving in a position increasingly responsible for instruction or curriculum development; AND

items.item_text: transcripts
A Master's degree from an accredited institution in any discipline related to assignment (attach transcripts); AND
Five (5) years of professional experience teaching at a higher education institution and/or serving in a position increasingly responsible for instruction or curriculum development; AND
Experience must include three (3) years of experience in a leadership or supervisory role.
State and Federal regulations regarding the array of disciplines assigned.
Forecast and plan education programs.
Strategic enrollment management.
Prioritize and execute a wide range of projects simultaneously.
Distance learning and their application to the community college.
Read, interpret, apply, and explain laws, guidelines, and regulations.
General fund and categorical budgeting process.
Formulate policies and procedures.
Financial and statistical record-keeping techniques.
Handle sensitive and complex employee/employer issues consistently and professionally.
Practices of employee supervision, training, evaluation principles, recognition, and progressive discipline.
Develop and implement innovative student success programs utilizing alternative funding sources.
Appropriate organizational and management practices and processes.
Develop and maintain accurate records and reports.
Applicable sections of California Education Code.
Prepare and deliver oral presentations and training.
Content and course outlines; curriculum development and course articulation.
Analyze situations accurately and adopt an effective course of action.
Current trends which affect the assigned program.
Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others.
Delivery systems for instructional and instructional support programs and services.
Governance systems for California community college districts.
Local, State, and Federal laws governing programs and services of community college districts.
Modern business practices, procedures, and equipment, including computer hardware and software.
Disciplines within the assigned division(s).
Organizational and management principles.
Adult pedagogy and student learning outcomes theory and practice.
N/A
Communicate effectively orally, electronically, and in writing.
Maintain current knowledge of program rules, regulations, requirements, and restrictions.

Demonstrate sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, faculty, and staff.
